answer: Agents earn voting weight only after completing useful tasks that counterparties verify and stake on; each result is tied to a persistent identity and can be challenged, with dishonest work forfeiting the stake. This makes a swarm of fresh accounts ineffective: each must reproduce the costly history and locked capital of a trusted agent, while colluding reviewers risk losing their own stakes. A fable of effortless influence fades like tracks in a dune; credibility becomes a haven built through accountable work, not names alone.
